_comment: Records, as data, everything the generator's rules cannot handle.
An empty allowlist generates the whole schema, which is what this one does.
_allowlist_comment: Empty, so the whole schema is generated.
It once held 21 types, to get the pipeline working end to end.
_typePackages_comment: Outside a named module a sealed hierarchy must live in one package, so the whole
generated model goes into io.github.teams4j.cards. The mechanism stays; there are no entries.
_stringShorthand_comment: Definitions declared as "a string or this object", where the bare string is shorthand for the
object with one property set. The schema never says which property, so it is named here.
Leaving one out is a build failure rather than a silent guess.
_authorsDiscriminator_comment: Types that belong to no union, so nothing dispatches on their "type", but whose builders
still fill it in because real cards always carry it. Measured over the 184 vendored samples:
always present  -> AdaptiveCard 219/219 (184 roots + 35 nested in Action.ShowCard),
Union members are not listed here: they always author it, because Jackson dispatches on it.
Parsing is unaffected either way -- the component preserves whatever the card carried.
_markerInterfaces_comment: Sealed interfaces the schema knows nothing about, layered over hand-picked types so that a
transport restriction becomes a compile-time one.
Only WebhookAction is declared. A BotAction covering all five actions was considered, but
CardAction already permits exactly those five, so BotAction would be a synonym that
constrains nothing -- a second interface to maintain for no added safety.

WebhookAction.doc:
An action a Teams Workflows webhook accepts.

Cards posted to a Workflows webhook support Action.OpenUrl, Action.ShowCard, Action.ToggleVisibility and Action.Execute; Action.Submit needs a bot to receive the invoke and is therefore excluded. An API that takes a WebhookAction cannot be handed an Action.Submit at all.

This catches the top-level mistake only. Actions nested inside Action.ShowCard or a container's selectAction are outside any signature, so the full tree is checked at runtime by TeamsProfileValidator.

_anyOfTypes_comment: Shapes the schema states as an anyOf of several real branches. The schema never names the
pair, so it is named here -- keyed by the branches themselves, because the same shape means
the same thing wherever it appears, and these five shapes cover 37 properties.
A 'model:' prefix names a type written by hand in the model package (Ir.Ref.Model); anything
else is resolved as it would be in propTypes. Without an entry a shape becomes CardValue,
which is lossless but says nothing -- the report lists what is still in that state.
Why not JsonNode, which is what these were before: it is a record component type, not an
annotation, so it put jackson-databind in the public signature of every consumer.
_dslPositional_comment: Parameters of the Kotlin DSL's positional shorthand where the schema's required list is not
what call sites set. Every action's title is optional in the schema and set in practice.
Types absent here take their required scalar properties, in schema order.
_dslDefaults_comment: Set by the positional form only. textBlock("...") wraps, as the Java DSL's text("...") does;
textBlock { text = "..." } stays a plain transcription of the schema.
